summary: Built a reusable retrieval-quality benchmark for search_knowledge (/search). Files (committed on attempt branch orch/attempt/a6a3552b...-3, commit 8a22d2c, repo /Users/imyu/.claude/orchestrator): bench/retrieval/eval-set.json (28 labeled query→relevant-note cases over the [ingest] KB, keyed on STABLE note titles not volatile ids, so it survives re-ingestion); scripts/retrieval-bench.js (hits live /search, computes recall@k/precision@k/MRR at configurable cutoffs → scorecard.json+md, with a --check regression gate); test/retrieval-quality.test.js (offline deterministic guard — rebuilds the injected corpus from bench/ingest fixtures, scores via daemon's exported scorer, asserts recall@5≥0.85 & MRR@5≥0.80, validates every relevant title exists). Tested: offline test 4/4 pass (recall@5=0.946, MRR@5=0.893); live bench PASS recall@5=0.911 precision@5=0.186 MRR@5=0.819 (28q); --check exit 0; pre-existing search-knowledge.test.js still 5/5. Finding: 1 zero-recall query ('converged-vs-iterate' note) — bag-of-words scorer misses it under live distractor load; left exposed by design, not patched. HELD FOR MERGE — main (0294f09) untouched, human gate.
